correctness.rationale: For any competitor B of k distinct primes, its maximal element b exceeds q/k and the product R of the other k-1 primes satisfies P_{k-1}<=R<kM, so k<=Λ(M), R<MΛ(M). Its remaining sum u<=R and s<=M yield |b-q|=|s-u|<MΛ(M). Prime isolation forces b=q; original product minimality then gives R=M and U=A by prime factorization. Empty U works; PNT gives asymptotic. Finite verifier gives VERIFY_OK but is not the universal proof.

value.rationale: A key prime-adjoining lemma in the recent resolution of an additive number theory problem needs an isolated prime. The new bound replaces a quadratic isolation width 4M^2 with H=MΛ(M)=(1+o(1))M log M/loglog M and gives an explicit computable cutoff, a scale-changing quantitative strengthening. This is a natural structural improvement, not an arbitrary slice or mere constant improvement.
